_comment: Èkó Ò Ní Bàjẹ́ (D-021, docs/story/eko-oni-baje.md). Missions with steps are playable; the rest are planned. Pidgin, Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa lines are flagged for native-speaker review. Brands are kept out: Bayo's phone is 'Papa's old phone', vehicles are unbranded.

acts.title: Act I · Hustle No Dey Sleep
Act II · No Condition Is Permanent
Act IV · The Hand That Feeds You
Act V · Èkó Ò Ní Bàjẹ́

missions.title: Oshodi, 2011
missions.summary: The night Chief Bayo dies. Hide, run through the market and remember: a lion-head walking stick and a voice saying "No witness".

steps.text: Oshodi, 2011
steps.sub: Rain. Generators humming under the bridge.

lines.text: (on the phone) I don show dem everything. Tomorrow, the press go hear am.
Headlights sweep the union office. Three pickups, no plates.
Dayo. Take this phone. Run. Go Mama. No look back.

steps.text: Papa's old phone
Stay down under the counter. Don't move.
Run through the market. Don't let them catch you.
Hide in the gutter under the bridge.
Don't move. Don't breathe.

lines.text: Bayo, you for just collect the money. Make una finish am.
No witness.
In Dayo's fist, Papa's old phone is still recording. Then the battery dies.

steps.text: ÈKÓ Ò NÍ BÀJẸ́

missions.title: "Obalende! Obalende!"
missions.summary: Danfo driving with Sego hanging off the door. Pick up fares, argue over change, and find a bag left behind.

lines.text: Sabi! You dey sleep for road? Obalende people don full ground!
I dey here, I dey here. Make we hustle.
Obalende! Obalende! Enter with your change o!

steps.text: Stop at a bus stop to load passengers, then drop them at the next stop (2 runs).

lines.text: Oga, I no get ₦200 change. Drop me for next bus stop.
Madam, change na your own wahala, no be ours!
Malaria, ulcer, bad luck: one bottle cure all! Five hundred naira only!
Oga herbal, abeg no sell bad luck inside my bus. We get enough.
Sabi, see bag for back seat. Somebody forget am.
UNILAG ID card. Tolu Adeyemi. This girl na Kemi classmate.
As our elders say... I no remember wetin dem say, but e go make sense later.

steps.text: Tolu Adeyemi's student ID

missions.title: Agbero Tax
missions.summary: Kongi's agberos demand double ticket. Dayo refuses. Then he sees the lion-head walking stick.

steps.text: Drive to Oshodi park for the evening load.

lines.text: Driver! Today ticket na double. Chairman orders.
Double? I pay this morning.
Morning na morning, evening na evening. Pay, or we scatter that bus.
Then come scatter am.

steps.text: Fight Wire and his boys. Passengers are placing bets.

lines.text: Across the park, a man watches from the office window, leaning on a lion-head walking stick.
...No witness.
Dayo freezes. Wire's knife catches his arm.
Sabi! Your hand! Ah, small wahala, small wahala. Make we comot here!

missions.title: One Chance
missions.summary: Chase a one-chance bus across the bridge, ram it and rescue Amaka from the robbers.

lines.text: Near the Third Mainland Bridge, a danfo full of 'passengers' swerves. A woman is fighting inside.
One chance bus. Not today.

steps.text: Chase the one-chance bus and ram it to a stop.
Fight the robbers on the shoulder, with traffic flying past.

lines.text: Thank you. Thank you. I sell aso-ebi for Balogun market. I just enter the wrong bus.
Aso-ebi seller wey dey carry camera?
Her bag has spilled open: a press card, and photos of Oshodi park buses at night.
Please. Forget wetin you see.
Lagos na place of secrets, madam. I no see anything.

steps.text: Seen: photos of Oshodi park buses at night

missions.title: The Chairman Will See You
missions.summary: Kongi offers ₦500,000 for a special load to the Seme border. Uncle Obi warns Dayo off "those park people".

steps.text: Kongi has summoned you. Go to the union office.

lines.text: Sabi. The boy wey beat my boys. Sit down.
I need driver wey get liver. ₦500,000 for one job: a special load of rice to the Seme border.
Dayo can't stop staring at the lion-head walking stick.
You like am? Gift from a big man. Lagos na place of gifts, Sabi.

steps.text: So? You dey in or you dey out?

lines.text: Chairman say make I give you this. Half now, half when you come back.

steps.reason: Kongi's advance for the Seme run

lines.text: (on the phone) Dayo, my son. I hear you dey move with those park people.
Stay away from them, you hear? Think of your sister. Think of Mama.
I hear you, Uncle Obi.

missions.title: Seme Run
missions.summary: A night convoy of smuggled rice. One sack moves: Tolu Adeyemi. Turn the convoy around.

steps.text: Seme Run

lines.text: (radio) Follow the escort. No stop for anybody. Customs see you, na your own palava.

steps.text: Follow the escort pickup. Don't fall behind.
Customs patrol on your tail! Make it to the border post.
Customs! Where una dey carry rice go this hour of night?

lines.text: In the back, one rice sack moves.
Rice no dey breathe.
He cuts it open. A gagged girl: Tolu Adeyemi, the girl from the ID card. Three more sacks hold people.
Please... please. They said we were going to Cotonou.

steps.text: Took a pistol from the cab's glovebox
The escorts turn on you. Take them down.
Get the four victims to the church in Badagry.

lines.text: The church doors open. The pastor counts four frightened faces and hides them in the vestry.
God bless you. Tell Kemi I'm alive.
You go tell am yourself.

missions.title: Eyo Day
missions.summary: Save Kongi from gunmen in the white-robed festival crowd, then get arrested by ACP Hauwa.

steps.text: Eyo Day
steps.sub: Lagos Island is a sea of white.

lines.text: No vehicles in the festival zone. Dayo wraps himself in a white agbada and walks in.

steps.text: Find Kongi in the crowd.

lines.text: Kongi! You and me need to talk.
Sabi? You come here to—
Shots crack from inside the white-robed crowd.

steps.text: Drag Kongi out through the Idumota alleys. The gunmen are dressed in white!

lines.text: (bleeding) Dem no come for me. Dem come make you look like say na you.
Oladayo Balogun. Hands where I can see them. You are under arrest.
I just saved this man's life!
Then you will have plenty to tell the judge.

steps.headline: EVENING NEWS
steps.text: Danfo driver's bus found burned "with evidence of human trafficking".

lines.text: In Mushin, Kemi watches the news and cries.
(on the phone) Don't worry, my daughter. I will handle it.

steps.text: END OF ACT I

missions.title: Cell Four
missions.summary: Hauwa's deal: a staged escape that a real hit squad turns deadly.

steps.text: Cell Four

lines.text: Cell Four. Forty men in a room built for ten, and one of them runs it.
New boy! Your people bring food? Na me dey chop first. Na me be president for here.
Please... na my mama food. I never chop since yesterday.
You dey argue with president? Oya, bring am.
Leave the boy alone.

steps.text: Stop the cell president.

lines.text: Thank you, sir. God go bless you.
(from the corner) That one na soldier. See as he dey fight.

steps.text: That night

lines.text: Balogun. Up. Quietly.
I know you freed those girls at Seme. The rice sacks. The church in Badagry.
So why am I in this cell?
Because somebody wanted you here. My brother Sadiq vanished from Oshodi park three years ago. Nobody looked for him. I am looking.
My deal: I stage your escape tonight. You go back inside, close to the people who move people. You tell me everything.

steps.text: Take ACP Hauwa's deal?
Follow Hauwa out of the cell.

lines.text: Through the yard. The gate is unlocked for five minutes. Run, and don't look back.

steps.text: Cross the station yard to the gate.

lines.text: Headlights at the gate. Men in plain clothes with rifles. This was not the plan.
Those are not my men! Take this!

steps.text: Hauwa slides you her service pistol
A hit squad! Survive the shootout in the compound.

between.text: More coming! Use the pickup for cover!

lines.text: (breathing hard) Somebody in my own command sent them. They were going to shoot you "while escaping".
Go. Call me on this number. Nobody else.
And if your somebody finds me first?
Then run faster.

steps.text: ACP Hauwa's private number
Get away from the station: lose them in the Yaba streets.

missions.title: Computer Village
missions.summary: Meet Bigz. A foot chase through the phone stalls for a stolen laptop.

steps.text: Computer Village
Meet Amaka at Computer Village.

lines.text: No more aso-ebi seller. I work for The Lagos Ledger. I've been following people who vanish from motor parks for a year.
You could have told me on the bridge.
You could have been one of them. This is Bigz. He can trace the phones from the Seme convoy.
Sabi! Correct guy. My fee is small: some Allen Avenue boys stole my laptop. Everything is inside. Help me collect am back.
Look, see am there! The one in the blue shirt!
Wahala! Na Bigz!

steps.text: He's gone up onto the shop roofs. Catch the laptop thief!

lines.text: Oga, no vex! Na dem send me!

steps.text: His friends climb up after you. Deal with them.
Bigz's laptop

lines.text: My baby! Give me two minutes.
Your Seme numbers... every one of them pings the same place on weekends. An event centre in Lekki.
Saturday is the senator's daughter's wedding there. Every big man in Lagos will be inside.
Then we're going to a wedding.

steps.text: The traced numbers

missions.title: Owambe
missions.summary: Infiltrate the senator's daughter's wedding in aso-ebi. Photograph the big men. Escape in the wedding convoy.

steps.text: Owambe

lines.text: Matching aso-ebi. Smile like you're family. Spray money, dance when the drummer calls, and keep away from the aunties.
The back room. That's where the big men meet. We need a photo of whoever goes in.
And the aunties?
They know everybody's face. Everybody's.

steps.text: Blend in at the owambe: spray money, dance when the drummer calls, dodge the aunties.
Slip to the back room window and photograph the meeting.
steps.got: Click. Wire, taking a fat envelope from the senator's aide.

lines.text: Tiamiyu "Wire", Kongi's lieutenant, takes an envelope from the senator's aide.
...Na who dey for window? NA YOU! SABI!
Run!

steps.text: Wire's men open fire under the canopy. Take cover behind the tables!

lines.text: (leaning out of the back with Dayo's pistol) Drive! I've got the camera and I've got their tyres!

steps.text: Escape the wedding convoy down the expressway to Ikoyi!

lines.text: Wire. Kongi's lieutenant. Taking the senator's money.
So it's Kongi.

steps.text: Photos from the back room

missions.title: Makoko
missions.summary: Canoe chase to a stilt house full of captives and red calabashes.

steps.text: Makoko
steps.sub: The stilt town on the lagoon

lines.text: (phone) Wire's phone is in Makoko. One house, far end, near the open water. It hasn't moved since morning.

steps.text: Wire's boys come at you in canoes through the water lanes. Sink them!
Paddle to the house at the far end of Makoko.

lines.text: Chained captives waiting for transport, and calabashes painted red.
Please... don't kill us.
I'm here to take you home. Who brought you?
The men say the Chairman of Oshodi go collect us. Tonight.

steps.text: Wire's men come up the ladder!

lines.text: (outside) Burn am! Burn everything!
Petrol splashes the walls. Fire.

steps.text: Get the captives out of the burning house to the canoe!

lines.text: The house sinks into the lagoon behind them. A bullet has found Dayo's side.
...I'm fine. Go. Go!

steps.text: A red calabash

lines.text: (phone) Dayo? You're bleeding? Listen to me. Go to Abeokuta. Baba Fakunle. Go now.

missions.title: Under Olumo Rock
missions.summary: Baba Fakunle heals Dayo and casts Ifá: the hand that washes your face dirtied it.

steps.text: Under Olumo Rock

lines.text: So this is Bayo's son. Lie down. The bullet is out; now the fever must go.
Baba Fakunle casts Ifá: the palm nuts fall.
The hand that washes your face is the same hand that dirtied it.
Riddles, Baba?
Your father was not killed over union politics. He found something, and he was going to the press. That is all Ifá will say today.

steps.text: Dawn
Climb Olumo Rock before the sun.

lines.text: At the top, the fever comes back as memory.
No witness.
Rain. A lion-head walking stick. A hand with a gold ring. A gutter, and a boy in it.
...I know that hand.

steps.text: Baba Fakunle's Ìrókò charm: some blows just don't land. Magic or adrenaline? Who knows.

lines.text: Go back to Lagos, son of Bayo. And look closely at those who love you.

missions.title: Third Mainland
missions.summary: Corner Kongi on the bridge. He didn't kill your father. A sniper kills him mid-sentence.

steps.text: Third Mainland

lines.text: Kongi. Tonight we finish this.
(radio, Kongi's boys) Sabi dey come for Papa! Stop am for bridge!

steps.text: Kongi's boys are on you. Weave through the bridge traffic!
Kongi's men are on that tanker. Get alongside it!
You leap from the okada onto the tanker!
Fight on top of the moving tanker!

lines.text: The tanker jack-knifes across the lanes. Kongi stumbles to the railing, the lagoon black below him.
(drops his gun) Sabi... Listen to me. I no kill your papa.
I carry your papa body for my hand. This stick? Dem dash me am one year after. Make e look like say na me.
The man wey dash me na—
A sniper's bullet. Kongi falls into Dayo's arms.
Headlights. Rasheed, Kongi's son, sees Dayo holding his father's body.
PAPA! You kill my papa! Sabi, you are a dead man!

steps.text: Run! Rasheed's boys are coming.

steps.headline: BREAKING
steps.text: Oshodi park chairman Alhaji Rasaki Adio shot dead on Third Mainland Bridge.
END OF ACT II

missions.title: Janazah
missions.summary: Kongi's burial. Rasheed gives Dayo eight days.

steps.text: Janazah
steps.sub: Oshodi. Kongi is buried before sunset.

lines.text: Dayo comes in a borrowed kaftan and cap, his head down. No gun. Not today.

steps.text: Get close to Rasheed at the graveside.

lines.text: Rasheed. I need to talk to you. I didn't—
(gun to Dayo's head) You come here? To my papa burial?
Not here. Not today. Put it down, my son.
...Eight days. After my papa Fidau prayer, I go find you. Run, Sabi.

steps.text: Walk out through the crowd. Don't fire a shot. Rasheed's boys are following.

lines.text: Eight days.

missions.title: Ballot Box
missions.summary: Election day. Snatch the boxes, or swap them and film it (Big Choice 1).

steps.text: Ballot Box
Join the park boys the senator's campaign is hiring.

lines.text: Listen. The opposition wards: the polling units by the stadium. Carry the boxes to the bus. Nobody gets hurt if nobody is stupid.
Fifty thousand each. Cash. Today.

steps.text: What does Dayo do with the ballot boxes?

options.text: Swap them for marked decoys, and film it all for Amaka (stealth)
Snatch them with the boys (big payout, the senator's people trust you)

lines.text: (earpiece) The decoys are in the blue bag. Swap the boxes in the truck and keep the phone recording.

then.text: Sneak to the box truck by the stadium and swap the boxes. Stay out of their sight.

then.got: Recording saved: faces, the bus, the aide counting cash.

else.text: The polling agents and their boys fight back.
Police! Get the boxes back to the collation centre.

lines.text: (counting notes into Dayo's hand) Good work. Oga Ọkpụ say make we take care of you.
Oga who?
Don't worry yourself. Big man. Very big man.

steps.headline: ELECTION DAY
steps.text: Violence and ballot snatching reported in several Lagos wards.

missions.title: LUTH
missions.summary: Race Sego's mother to theatre through gridlock.

steps.text: LUTH

lines.text: Sabi... my mama. The doctors say surgery today today, or... I no get the money. I no get anything.
Take it. All of it.
(crying) Sabi, na you be my brother. Anything. Anything.
Sego's mother is in the back. Rush hour has the whole mainland standing still.

steps.text: Race Sego's mother to LUTH through the go-slow!

lines.text: We'll take her from here. Theatre is ready.
God bless you, Sabi.
(Behind them, a man in a campaign cap steps up to the doctor and leans close.)

missions.title: Durbar
missions.summary: Chase the ring's trucks through the Sallah Durbar. Find Sadiq alive.

steps.text: Durbar

lines.text: (phone) The cattle trucks leave Lagos full and come back empty. This week they're in Kano, hiding in the Durbar crowds.
My cousin Musa. He rides for the emir.
Can you ride, Lagos boy?
I can drive anything.
A horse is not a danfo. Hold on with your knees.

steps.text: There! The cattle truck! Ride after it through the Durbar!
The truck's guards turn on you at the airstrip.

lines.text: Inside the truck: fourteen people. One of them looks up.
...Hauwa?
Sadiq. Sadiq! Allah, Sadiq!
Hauwa breaks down in Dayo's arms.
The buyers are foreigners. But the seller... an Igbo businessman. They call him Ọkpụ.

steps.text: Sadiq's testimony

missions.title: Kpo-Fire
missions.summary: General Tonye remembers the soldier who refused to burn his village.

steps.text: Kpo-Fire

lines.text: (to himself) Okoroba. I swore I'd never come back to these creeks.
(phone) The money goes through General Tonye's refineries. Find him.

steps.text: Take the speedboat through the mangroves to General Tonye's camp.

lines.text: Who send you here? You come to die?
...Wait. Wait. I know this face.
Na you be the soldier wey refuse burn Okoroba. My mama still dey alive because of you.
Engines on the water. The senator's hired mercenaries.
Dem follow you! Oya, enter boat!

steps.text: Tonye throws you a rifle magazine
Speedboat battle through the mangroves! Sink the mercenaries.

lines.text: A stray round finds the refinery's tanks.
(watching the creek burn) Your senator na puppet. The man wey dey hold the rope dey Alaba. Na trader, not politician.

steps.text: General Tonye's word

missions.title: Alaba International
missions.summary: Uncle Obi's safe house is raided. Mama Àgbà is shot. Kemi is taken.

steps.text: Alaba International
Go to Uncle Obi. The only man who has never failed the family.

lines.text: Uncle. They're coming for us. The ring, the senator... a trader in Alaba is behind it all.
(horrified) In MY market? Dayo... come here. Come here, my son.
He hugs him for a long time.
Nobody touches my sister's children. I have a house in Festac. Take Mama and Kemi there tonight. Money, guns, anything.

steps.text: Uncle Obi's guns

lines.text: Uncle Obi did all this for us? See, Dayo. Family.
(her iron box on her knees, as always) Sit, Dayo. For one night, let us be a family that is not afraid.
I bring food! Jollof and chicken. How una dey?
Sego! Who told you we were here?
(a beat) ...Sabi tell me now. Abi?

steps.text: That night

lines.text: Engines in the street. Men in police uniform pour through the gate.

steps.text: Defend the safe house!

lines.text: A last shot from the dark. Mama Àgbà falls.
MAMA! No, no, no...
(pointing at her iron box) Wo ọwọ́ tó ń bọ́ ẹ... Look at the hand that feeds you...
In the yard, Kemi screams. They drag her into a van.
Hauwa runs in, in full uniform, the same badge as the raiders.
Dayo! Wait—
You! YOU!

steps.text: Trust no one. Run.
Mama Àgbà's iron box
END OF ACT III

missions.title: Sego
missions.summary: Hunt down the informant. Kill Sego or let him go.

steps.text: Sego

lines.text: Mama Àgbà is buried in Mushin. Everybody comes. Sego does not.
He knew where we were. Only Sego knew.

steps.text: Hunt Sego through Ajegunle: the beer parlour.

lines.text: Sabi... Sabi, I fit explain—
He runs.

steps.text: Sego is up on the rooftops. Don't let him get away!

lines.text: (through tears) Dem pay for my mama surgery! Then dem say the doctor go "make mistake" if I no tell them where you dey hide.
I no know say dem go shoot Mama. I swear to God. I swear!

steps.text: Sego is on his knees at the edge of the roof.

options.text: Let him go. "Get out of Lagos."
Mama is dead because of him.

lines.text: Go. Get out of my sight. If you ever pray, pray for Mama.
I go make am up to you. I swear, Sabi.
The beer parlour's music is loud. Nobody hears anything.
Dayo walks down alone.

missions.title: Papa's Phone
missions.summary: Mama Àgbà's iron box. Bigz restores the recording. The voice is Uncle Obi's.

steps.text: Papa's Phone
Open Mama Àgbà's iron box.

lines.text: Inside: Chief Bayo's handwritten ledger of buses "borrowed" by the ring. Photographs. And, wrapped in a handkerchief, a tiny memory card.
From Papa's phone. Mama, you kept it fifteen years...

steps.text: Papa's ledger
The memory card from Papa's phone

lines.text: Old card, old phone. Give me one hour.
(Over black) Rain. Gunshots.
Bayo, you for just collect the money. Make una finish am. No witness.
(in Igbo, to someone else) Ọ dị mma. Give Rasaki the stick next year. Let them look at him.
I ran the voice against every voice I have. Radio adverts too.
One match. Chief Obinna Nwankwo. "Ọkpụ of Alaba".
Uncle Obi.
The man who paid Kemi's fees. The man who bought NO KING AS GOD. The man who has Kemi now.

steps.text: Mushin, night

lines.text: Sabi! Welcome o. How Mama? We never see am for market this week.

steps.text: From a shop radio: "Okpu Electronics, Alaba International! Chief Obinna Nwankwo, your brother in business. E no dey spoil!"
Walk home.

missions.title: Badge
missions.summary: Hauwa was never the enemy. Escape CP Ladipo's raid in a stolen city bus.

steps.text: Badge
Hauwa wants to meet. Alone.

lines.text: Hauwa puts her gun on the table first.
I got the tip-off too late. I came to stop it. The raiders in uniform were CP Ladipo's men. My commissioner. He is on Ọkpụ's payroll.
He has declared me wanted this morning.
So now we are both fugitives.
Alliance of outcasts.
Ladipo's unit! They followed me. Through the market, go!

steps.text: Fighting retreat through Yaba market!

lines.text: A city bus? Seriously?
I drive anything with wheels.

steps.text: Lose Ladipo's men in the stolen city bus!

missions.title: Brotherhood
missions.summary: Play the recording over the park loudspeaker. Rasheed joins. Assemble the crew.

steps.text: Brotherhood
steps.sub: Oshodi. The eight days are up.

lines.text: Every agbero in Oshodi. Rasheed in front. Dayo walks in unarmed.

steps.text: Walk into the park. Unarmed.

lines.text: You get mind. Talk your last talk.
Not my talk. My father's. Listen.
The union loudspeaker crackles. The recording plays across the whole park.
Make una finish am. No witness... Give Rasaki the stick next year. Let them look at him.
Silence across Oshodi.
(lowering his gun) ...Na the same man kill both our papa.
Oshodi dey with you, Sabi.

steps.text: The crew
Rasheed: "Every danfo for Oshodi go block road when you say."
General Tonye: "My boatmen dey ready. Lagos lagoon na small water."
Bigz: "Give me the distribution company's password and I fit off light for the whole of Ikoyi."
Hauwa: "Sadiq will testify. With the ledger, I can arrest Ladipo myself."
Amaka: "When it happens, The Lagos Ledger goes live."

then.text: A text from an unknown number: "I dey Lagos still. Anything you need. — S"

steps.text: The crew

missions.title: Iri Ji
missions.summary: Rescue Kemi during the New Yam festival among the masquerades.

steps.text: Iri Ji
steps.sub: The New Yam festival, Obinna's village

lines.text: Today Obinna takes the community's highest title and breaks the first yam before the whole town. Kemi is in his cellar.
(in a masquerade attendant's raffia) Nobody looks twice at the man who walks behind a masquerade.

steps.text: Slip from the festival to the mansion. Avoid the guards.
The cellar guard.

lines.text: Dayo! Uncle Obi will kill them when he knows—
Kemi. It's him. Uncle Obi is Ọkpụ.
No. No, you're lying. He paid my fees. He—
(from the balcony) Kemi-Kemi! My Ada! Where are you going with that boy?
...Uncle?
(to his men) Shoot the car.
(barely a whisper) It's true.

steps.text: Escape through the yam farms under fire!

lines.text: A helicopter lifts off from the mansion and turns south, towards Lagos.

steps.headline: BREAKING
steps.text: Senator Coker-Bankole declared governor-elect. Victory gala tomorrow night at his Banana Island home.

lines.text: He'll be there. Before they both fly out.
Then so will we.

steps.text: Kemi, safe
END OF ACT IV

missions.title: Blackout
missions.summary: Bigz kills the power. Sneak through dark estates between generator lights.

steps.text: Blackout

lines.text: (radio) Three. Two. One.
The whole of Ikoyi and Banana Island goes dark. Generators roar on, one after another. All but one.
(radio) The senator's gateman took the suya and the money. His generator is dead.

steps.reason: The gateman's carton of suya and ₦50,000 (3D)

steps.text: Sneak through the dark estate. Avoid the torches and the generators' light.

lines.text: From the wall, Dayo sees the roof: the senator's helicopter, rotors turning slowly.
(radio) They're not leaving tomorrow. They're leaving tonight. Everybody, now!

missions.title: Lagos Rises
missions.summary: Land, water and law: the crew hits everything at once while Dayo storms the gala.

steps.text: Lagos Rises
LAND · Rasheed: "Danfo don block every road round the estate, and the exits off Third Mainland. Nobody dey pass!"
WATER · Tonye: "My boys don cut the private jetty. Anything wey float, na we get am."
LAW · Amaka: "We are live on The Lagos Ledger. ACP Hauwa Danjuma is walking into the police command..."

lines.text: Gala guests in agbada and gele. Money still on the floor from the spraying. Then the guards see Dayo.

steps.text: Storm the mansion!

between.text: (radio) LIVE: CP Ladipo is in handcuffs! Hauwa did it!

steps.headline: LIVE · THE LAGOS LEDGER
steps.text: CP Ladipo arrested on air. Sadiq Danjuma's testimony and a dead man's ledger read out in full.

lines.text: (on his knees) Please! Please, I'm only a politician! It was Ọkpụ, it was all Ọkpụ!
Behind him, through the window, the helicopter lifts off from the roof.
Obinna?
He's not on it. The yacht. The jetty. He said: "Tell my nephew I'll be waiting for him."

missions.title: The Lion Staff
missions.summary: The yacht, the rain, the staff. Take it, drag him to shore, or walk away (Big Choice 2).

steps.text: The Lion Staff

lines.text: The yacht's lights head for open water. The skyline is lit only by generators.

steps.text: Obinna's gunboats! Sink them and catch the yacht.

lines.text: A shot from the yacht's stern. A fishing canoe cuts across. Sego, in the canoe, takes the bullet meant for Dayo.
(clutching his shoulder, laughing) Sabi... we don dey even.
Sego! You fool. You beautiful fool.
(the lion staff in his hand: he took it back from Kongi's grave) Your father was my brother too. He wanted to bring police into my business.
Lagos eats righteous men, Dayo. I fed your family for fifteen years. Your bus? Mine. Your sister's books? Mine.
You are standing on my money.

steps.text: Fight Obinna on the yacht deck. Watch the staff!

lines.text: Obinna is on the deck, beaten. The yacht is taking water. The lion staff rolls to Dayo's feet.

steps.text: Dayo holds the staff over his uncle.

options.text: Take the staff. The city's power passes to you.
Drag him to shore. Hand him to Hauwa alive.
Walk away. Leave him to the lagoon. Take Kemi and go.

lines.text: Dayo brings the staff down. Obinna's body goes into the dark lagoon.

steps.text: Six months later

lines.text: Dayo is chairman of Oshodi. He owns Obinna's Alaba warehouses. The new governor's office calls him "Oga". Danfos are painted with his face.
Kemi visits his office. She sees the lion-head staff on his desk.
She leaves without a word.
Dayo looks out at Oshodi: the same window Kongi once watched him from.

steps.text: ỌBA ÌTA

lines.text: Dayo drags Obinna to shore and hands him to Hauwa, alive.
Amaka's ballot footage, Bayo's ledger and the recording from his phone go public together.

steps.headline: ELECTION ANNULLED
steps.text: Obinna Nwankwo and CP Ladipo to stand trial. ACP Danjuma to lead a new police unit.

lines.text: Oshodi elects Dayo chairman in a fair vote. He repaints the union office in his father's colours.

steps.text: ÌDÁJỌ́

lines.text: (Months later, a sealed envelope arrives on the trial judge's desk. It carries the stamp of the Alaba traders' union.)
Dayo hands Obinna to Hauwa, alive.
But Obinna's lawyers have Dayo's own election-day footage: Sabi, snatching ballot boxes with the park boys. They paint him as a thug.

steps.headline: COURT
steps.text: Alaba businessman Obinna Nwankwo granted bail. "A political witch-hunt," says his counsel.

lines.text: On the courthouse steps, Obinna smiles at Dayo.
(Over black: a danfo engine starts.)

steps.text: ÌDÁJỌ́

lines.text: Dayo walks away and lets the lagoon decide.
Where are we going?
Across.

steps.text: Drive Kemi through the Seme border at dawn.
Months later

lines.text: Kemi is studying abroad. Dayo stayed in Cotonou a while, then came back to sit on Badagry beach and watch the Lagos skyline.
His phone rings. Rasheed.
Sabi, Oshodi need you.
Dayo smiles, doesn't answer. His father's old phone ringtone plays on.

steps.text: JAPA
